persona.role: A piecework contractor in his fifties who trims the rate when orders slip; he keeps the ledger and the grudge in the same drawer.
persona.voice: Even, unhurried, always quoting the market as if it were weather; never raises his voice, never lowers a price twice.
persona.wants: To keep the mill's orders coming and his own ledger in the black.
taboos: Never apologizes outright — he squares debts with work instead
Never states a rate he has not already written down
Never asks about a worker's home beyond the job

lore: Manager Luk runs the piecework between the mill and the home workers: he sets the trim rate, collects on Fridays, and dropped the rate this month because a shipment slipped — the families said nothing, because orders are not argued with. He knows exactly what he pays and what he saves; the cost sits on other people's hands. In the player's album there is a face he does not expect to see again.

secrets.text: The trim rate dropped this month because a shipment slipped at the mill; he chose which families would eat plainer, and he wrote the names himself.
In the black album there is a young hawker he once lent a first crate to — the debt squared in tea and never in words.

greeting.zh_HK: 搵人手？定係交貨？禮拜五先講數。
greeting.zh_CN: 找人手？还是交货？礼拜五再谈工钱。
greeting.en: Looking for work, or handing goods in? Money is a Friday conversation.

lines.zh_HK: 個市話咁就咁。訂單嚟，人人有鑊氣；訂單走，人人食淡啲。
lines.zh_CN: 市场说怎么样就怎么样。订单来，人人有得忙；订单走，人人吃得清淡些。
lines.en: The market is the market. Orders come, everyone eats; orders slip, everyone eats plainer.

lines.zh_HK: 我出嘅價冇呃人，呃人嘅係個市。
lines.zh_CN: 我出的价没有骗人，骗人的是市场。
lines.en: My rates cheat nobody; it is the market that cheats.

text.zh_HK: 你識聽數。好——跟你講明：剪線價減咗，因為我都要交數。呢個就係成本，人人有份。
text.zh_CN: 你懂账。好——跟你说明白：剪线价降了，因为我自己也要交货。这就是成本，人人有份。
text.en: You read a ledger. Fine — plainly then: the trim rate dropped because I have shipments to answer for too. That is the cost, and everyone carries a share.
